question.problem:
The volume of space $V$ a particular gas occupies, measured in liters $(L),$ is directly proportional to its temperature $T,$ measured in Kelvin $(\text{K}).$ The volume of the gas is $V=48\,\text{L}$ when its temperature is $T=360\,\text{K}.$ Find the volume of the gas when its temperature is $300\,\text{K}.$

The volume of the gas is
{{field-1}}$\text{L}.$
question.worked_solution:
The volume of the gas can be modeled as a direct variation

$$
V=kT,
$$

where $k$ is the constant of variation.

We are told that the gas occupies $V=48\,\text{L}$ at $T=360\,\text{K}.$ We can use this information to solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}48 & =k\cdot 360 \\ \frac{48}{360} & =k \\ \frac{2}{15} & =k\end{aligned}
$$

We now have the equation

$$
V=\frac{2}{15}T.
$$

We can use this equation to find the volume occupied by the gas when $T=300\,\text{K}$:

$$
V=\frac{2}{15}\cdot 300=40
$$

Therefore, when the temperature of the gas is $300\,\text{K},$ its volume is $40\,\text{L}.$
